name: Supermarkets and hypermarkets

problems.words: Bread and dairy expire on the shelf because we over-order every day
quick_ideas: Write down leftover bread and dairy by item for a week, so orders can follow real sales instead of a fixed quantity
Compare weekday and weekend leftovers, because the same order every day rarely fits both.

workzap_build.text: suggested daily order quantities for bread, dairy and produce worked out from recent sales by weekday, with near-expiry alerts.

problems.ask_first: Who decides the daily order today?
problems.free_stops: How order quantities are calculated and when alerts fire are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each day's bread and dairy order with that night's leftovers, so you spot which items are being routinely over-bought.
Give one person the daily bread and dairy order sheet, so ordering follows one clear record instead of habit.

problems.words: Fresh produce wastage is huge and nobody records it
quick_ideas: Weigh what each fresh section throws out for a few days, so you see which items cost the most
Note the reason (overripe, damaged, unsold), because each reason has a different fix.

workzap_build.text: a phone wastage log by section, item and reason with photos, and a weekly cost total for the owner.

problems.ask_first: Which fresh section worries you most?
problems.free_stops: The wastage categories and weekly report layout are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many crates each produce section throws out by closing time, so the heaviest wastage area gets attention first.
Give one supervisor one wastage notebook by the back door, so every throwout is noted in the same place.

problems.words: Shelves look empty in the evening even though the godown is full
quick_ideas: Walk the aisles before the evening rush and note empty facings, so you see which aisles fall behind
Give named staff named aisles, so refilling isn't everyone's and no one's job.

workzap_build.text: a shelf-gap check on phone where empty facings become refill tasks, assigned and timed every day.

problems.ask_first: When do shelves usually go empty?
problems.free_stops: The aisle check routine and task timings are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which shelves sit empty longest during the evening walk, so you see where refilling keeps breaking down.
Give one staff member the evening godown handover list, so refills reach the floor before shoppers face gaps.

problems.words: Receivers sign GRNs without counting cartons
quick_ideas: Count a few deliveries against the order yourself, so you know how often short delivery happens
Photograph any damaged delivery before the driver leaves, so claims have proof.

workzap_build.text: a receiving check on phone against the PO that records shortages and damage and tracks each distributor claim until credited.

problems.ask_first: How many deliveries come in on a typical day?
problems.free_stops: The receiving steps and the claims tracking are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare cartons received with cartons signed for on a few deliveries, so short counts stop being hidden by quick signatures.
Give one receiver the carton count on every delivery, so signing happens after a physical check each time.

problems.words: Cashiers' tills are short at night almost every day
quick_ideas: Count tills at shift change for a few days, so the gap points to a shift
Look at voids done after the customer has left, because these often explain gaps.

workzap_build.text: till reconciliation per cashier code and shift, with void and refund exceptions flagged every day.

problems.ask_first: Is it spread across tills or mostly certain shifts?
problems.free_stops: The exception rules and how they are reported are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each cashier's handwritten sales total with the till cash before closing for one week, so the mismatch point shows up earlier.
Keep one notebook at the cash office for every shortage note before handover, so night teams stop arguing over missing cash.

problems.words: Price changed at the distributor but the shelf label still shows old rate
quick_ideas: Spot-check a handful of labels against the POS, so you know how widespread it is
Keep one list of the week's price changes, so POS and labels are updated from the same source.

workzap_build.text: a price-change flow from new distributor rate to POS update to label print list and sign-off.

problems.ask_first: How do you hear about distributor rate changes today?
problems.free_stops: The steps and sign-offs in the price-change flow are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare distributor price changes with shelf labels during one aisle walk, so you see which categories are drifting most.
Give one person one weekly price-change list, so shelf labels and selling rates are updated from the same note.

problems.words: Basket size is small, people come for milk and leave
quick_ideas: Put everyday companions like bread and eggs near milk, because people pick up what they pass
Look at a few days of receipts to see what regulars usually buy together.

workzap_build.text: a customer list (with their permission) showing visits and baskets, and WhatsApp offers sent straight to regulars.

problems.ask_first: Do you already run a loyalty card?
problems.free_stops: Which offers go to which customers and how baskets are tracked are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Watch what milk buyers add to their baskets during one busy period, so you see the natural companion items in your store.
Give one staff member the job of refilling milk companions together, so shoppers keep seeing the add-on items nearby.

problems.words: Pandamart/Talabat orders come in and pickers can't find items
quick_ideas: Note why each problem order went wrong for a week, so you see whether it's stock, picking or substitutions
Sort picking lists by aisle, so pickers walk the store once.

workzap_build.text: Delivery-service and WhatsApp orders would land in one queue with aisle-sorted picking lists, and substitutions would be logged and shared with the customer.

problems.ask_first: Which channels do you take orders from?
problems.free_stops: How orders from each channel are pulled in and picked is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many picker delays come from missing shelf stock versus missing back stock, so the real blockage becomes visible.
Give one picker one problem list during each shift, so missing items are handed over for refill without delay.

problems.words: Freezer breaks down and we lose stock before anyone notices
quick_ideas: Put a temperature sheet on each chiller and freezer, so a failing unit shows up before stock is lost
Book servicing before summer, because breakdowns cluster in heat.

workzap_build.text: a chiller and freezer log on phone with alerts when a reading is missed or out of range.

problems.ask_first: How many chillers and freezers do you run?
problems.free_stops: The reading schedule and alert limits are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which freezer is warmest at opening and closing this week, so you spot the unit that keeps drifting.
Give one staff member the opening and closing freezer check, so problems are noticed early and passed on fast.

problems.words: We don't know what to stock up on before Ramadan
quick_ideas: Pull last Ramadan's sales for your top items once, so buying starts from facts
Confirm supplier lead times now, so stock lands before the rush.

workzap_build.text: a Ramadan and Eid stock planner from last year's sales by item and week, updated as this year's sales come in.

problems.ask_first: Does your POS keep last year's sales by item?
problems.free_stops: How the planner uses past sales and lead times is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count which staples customers ask for most during this week, so Ramadan buying reflects real demand from your own floor.
Give one buyer one notebook for Ramadan stock notes, so supplier calls and shop requests stay aligned each day.

never_say: Anything on food safety, hygiene certification, halal or food-licence rules.
How to relabel, re-date or repackage expired goods.
Ways around official price lists or price controls.
That shoplifters should be held or confronted; for food poisoning, gas or fire, go to the authorities or emergency services first.
That a change will cut wastage or raise margin by any amount.

sample_reply.person: Our bakery and dairy wastage is out of control. We throw away so much every night. Can you suggest a solution?
sample_reply.pi:
Yes, there is a way through this, and none of it needs special equipment.
First, have the closing supervisor write down leftover bread and dairy by item for a week, so the order follows what actually sold.
Second, compare weekday and weekend leftovers, because one fixed quantity rarely fits both.
The next step up would be: a phone wastage log and a suggested daily order for bread, dairy and produce worked out from recent sales, with near-expiry alerts.

Shall I have a solution document and quote prepared for you? You're free to say no.
